pages.title: In Pics: 2027 Triumph Tiger 1200 Launched In India
pages.meta_description: Triumph has launched the new Triumph 1200 in India with fresh looks, a more powerful engine and advanced features. Here is more about it:
headings: Triumph has launched the 2027 Tiger 1200 in India in two variants, GT Pro and Rally Explorer.
The GT Pro is priced at Rs 20.99 lakh (ex-showroom, Delhi) and is a road-focused variant and comes in Sapphire Black and Aluminium Silver/Pacific Blue colours.
The GT Pro gets cast aluminium alloy wheels, a 20-litre fuel tank and weighs 250 kg kerb,
The Rally Explorer is priced at Rs 23.49 lakh (ex-showroom, Delhi) and has off-road-focused features and hardware and comes in Ash Grey/Sapphire Black and Matt Khaki Green shades.
The Rally Explorer gets tubeless spoke wheels, a 30-litre fuel tank, Off-road Pro mode, engine guards, TPMS and 268 kg kerb weight.
It retains the 1,160 cc engine with revised internal components and gearing, and it now makes 130 Nm and 158 PS, 8 PS more than before.
This ultimate ADV gets semi-active Showa EERA heightflex suspension, which lowers the seat height by 30 mm when the bike comes to a halt.
The bike has twin discs at the front with Brembo Stylema calipers and a single rear disc.
It is feature-loaded with a 7-inch TFT console with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, an air-cooled phone storage on the tank, heated grips and a centre stand assist.
The Tiger has a front and rear Bosch radar system for adaptive cruise control, blind-spot assist, forward collision warning and emergency brake assist.

pages.title: Honda NS125FX Freedom Gundam Launched Internationally
pages.meta_description: Honda has launched the limited edition NS125FX Freedom Gundam edition in China, and here is everything this anime-themed scooter gets:
headings: Honda has launched the limited-edition NS125FX Freedom Gundam edition in China.
This 125 cc scooter is based on the anime Mobile Suit Gundam SEED.
It was first showcased at Bilibili World 2026 in China, which is an anime and gaming expo.
It gets the white colour with red and blue accents and ZGMF-X10A Freedom Gundam graphics on side panels.
The wheels are painted red and blue, and the front of the seat gets the Gundam Seed logo and anime-inspired graphics all over the scooter.
It is powered by a 124 cc air-cooled engine making 9.5 PS at 7,750 rpm and 10 Nm at 5,750 rpm
The fuel tank capacity is 5.7 litres with a claimed mileage of 50 kmpl.
This scooter features a coloured LCD console, USB-A and USB-C charging ports and single-channel ABS.
The seat height is 740 mm, and the scooter weighs 106 kg kerb.

pages.title: Royal Enfield X Hedon Limited Edition Helmets Launched
pages.meta_description: Royal Enfield and Hedon collaborated to create two limited-edition, handcrafted helmets. Here is everything you need to know:
headings: Royal Enfield has collaborated with Hedon, a British premium helmet maker, to launch a handcrafted limited-edition helmet collection.
The collection has two helmets: the Hedonist, a half-face, and the Heroine Racer 2.0 full-face.
These helmets are limited to only 16 units worldwide, each handcrafted to order and numbered.
These helmets are created to celebrate 125 years of Royal Enfield.
The half-face hedonist helmet costs GBP 1,650 (approx. Rs 2.11 lakh) and comes in six sizes, XS to XXL, weighing between 850 and 1,000 grams
The full-face helmet costs GBP 2,100 (approx. Rs 2.68 lakh) and comes in six sizes, S to XXXL, weighing between 1,200 and 1,390 grams
Both the helmets are ECE22.06 and DOT certified and come with a 1-year standard warranty.
Each helmet is made out of a composite shell of fibreglass and carbon fibre.
The Hedonist has Merlin anti-bacterial fabric, a stainless steel double-D fastener, a 3-channel ventilation system, and 7 additional interchangeable coloured visors.

pages.title: In Pics: Honda CB 500 Image Gallery
pages.meta_description: Honda has launched its retro roadster, the CB 500, in India. Take a closer look at this bike through detailed images:
headings: Honda launched the all-new CB500 in India, starting at Rs 2,75,000 (ex-showroom, Delhi).
The bike is available in three variants: the base Alloy variant, the Spoke variant for Rs 2,99,900 and Spoke With Stripes at Rs 3,01,900 (all prices are ex-showroom, Delhi)
The CB500 comes in five shades: Pearl Igneous Black, Rebel Red Metallic, Mat Steel Silver Metallic, Pearl Deep Ground Gray, and Pearl Igneous Black with stripes.
The bike is powered by a 502 cc single-cylinder, air and oil-cooled engine.
This engine produces 28.1 PS and 43.3 Nm.
It gets a round LED headlight, teardrop-shaped fuel tank, single-piece seat and brushed aluminium engine casing, giving it a classic roadster look.
Underpinnings include a telescopic front fork and twin rear shock setup.
Wheels are alloys or tubeless cross-spoke units with a 19-inch front and 18-inch rear setup and disc brakes at both ends.
It features an analogue speedometer with a small digital inset with Bluetooth connectivity for navigation and call/SMS alerts.

pages.title: 2026 Bajaj Pulsar 220F Explained: In Images
pages.meta_description: 2026 Bajaj Pulsar 220F updated with an LED headlamp and a new colour: Here's all you need to know in detailed images
headings: The Bajaj Pulsar 220F has received an update for 2026, finally getting an LED headlamp and a new colour option.
The bike looks a bit more modern now.
It still gets a semi-fairing, clip-on handlebars, and a split seat with split grab rails.
The bike is available in four colour options: Black Gold, Black Cherry Red, Black Ink Blue, and Black Copper Beige.
The new Black Gold colour option gets a black base paint with attractive gold graphics, along with carbon-fibre stickers, giving the bike a premium touch.
The Black Cherry Red colour gets a black base paint with bright red graphics. This colour is great for someone who likes attention.
The Black Ink Blue colour gets blue graphics on the tank and the semi-fairing, making it look sporty and youthful.
The Black Copper Beige colour gets copper graphics that look stealthy. It is perfect for someone who wants an understated look.
Powering the bike is a 220cc oil-cooled engine producing 20.9PS and 18.6Nm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox.
The bike is equipped with telescopic forks and twin shock absorbers at the rear, along with dual disc brakes.
The bike gets a digital instrument console with Bluetooth connectivity, all-LED lighting and a USB charging port, but misses out on a gear position indicator.
The bike gets single-channel ABS as standard.

pages.title: CFMoto V4 SR-RR Makes A New Top Speed Record: In Pics
pages.meta_description: The CFMoto V4 SR-RR recently made a new record for China, after achieving an impressive top speed during test runs at the Shangrao proving ground:
headings: The V4 SR-RR is a superbike from CFMoto, that clocked an impressive top speed of 315.82kmph at the Shangrao proving ground in China.
The bike was first unveiled at EICMA 2025, and is still in the testing phase.
Its top speed is now said to be a new record for a Chinese production engine.
The CFMoto V4 SR-RR uses a 997cc V4 engine, producing 210PS and 115Nm.
It is easily one of the most striking looking superbikes in the world, with aggressive styling, and sharp body panels.
The bike also gets quite large winglets at the front, which improves aerodynamics, and also improves the overall stance of the bike.
It also gets a single sided swing arm, which completes its overall aesthetic package.
It gets a lightweight aluminium frame, with the engine being a stressed member, and runs on lightweight forged aluminium 17-inch wheels.
Other than this, the V4 SR-RR is also expected to come loaded with all the rider's aids, and safety features.

pages.title: Hero Splendor & HF Deluxe Flex Fuel: Launched In Images
pages.meta_description: Hero MotoCorp launches the Splendor Flex Fuel and HF Deluxe Flex Fuel in India. Check prices, engine details, ethanol compatibility and more.
headings: Hero MotoCorp has launched the E85-compliant Splendor Flex Fuel and HF Deluxe Flex Fuel in India
Both motorcycles can run on fuel containing up to 85 percent ethanol (E85)
The Splendor Flex Fuel is priced at Rs 82,810, while the HF Deluxe Flex Fuel costs Rs 72,792 (ex-showroom, Delhi)
The Splendor Flex Fuel commands a premium of Rs 2,479 over the regular top-end Splendor Plus
The HF Deluxe Flex Fuel is just Rs 172 more expensive than the regular top-end HF Deluxe
Both bikes feature new graphics and exclusive colour schemes to distinguish them from standard models
The Splendor Flex Fuel’s 97.2cc engine produces 8.57PS and 8.3Nm, making it slightly more powerful than the regular version
The HF Deluxe Flex Fuel uses the same ethanol-compatible engine and delivers similar power and torque figures
Suspension, chassis, and braking hardware remain unchanged from the standard commuter motorcycles

pages.title: Royal Enfield Bullet 650: Review In Images
pages.meta_description: Here’s the review of the recently launched Royal Enfield Bullet 650 with the help of detailed real-life images
headings: The Bullet 650 is Royal Enfield’s biggest upgrade yet to its iconic old-school cruiser formula
Retains classic Bullet styling with 3D tank badges, peashooter exhausts, and squared-off mudguards
Gets premium detailing like hand-painted gold pinstriping and excellent overall build quality
Powered by the familiar 648cc parallel-twin engine with a relaxed and highly tractable character
The bike feels happiest cruising calmly, comfortably pulling from as low as 50kmph in sixth gear
Highway performance is effortless, with relaxed cruising possible between 80-120kmph
Has mild vibrations on the seat, handlebar and footpegs at 100kmph which increase as the speed increases
Despite its 243kg kerb weight, the low centre of gravity makes it surprisingly manageable in traffic
Ride quality is comfortable and more relaxed than the Classic 650 thanks to revised ergonomics
Returns a tested real-world mileage of 20.2kmpl with a range of around 290km per tank
Features include dual-channel ABS, Tripper navigation pod, adjustable levers, and a USB charging port
Tubeless spoke wheels are notably missing despite the bike’s strong touring-focused nature

pages.title: In 10 Images: TVS Jupiter 125 New Colours Launched
pages.meta_description: TVS has launched two new colour schemes for DT SXC variant of Jupiter 125
headings: TVS launched two new shades for the Jupiter 125 - Ivory Matte Copper Bronze and Ivory Elite Green.
These new colours are added to the DT SXC variant, which now has four colour options, including Ivory brown and Ivory Grey.
The Ivory Matte Copper Bronze gets a copper-coloured apron, front fender and side panels and white colour on the sides of the apron, floorboard, flyscreen and above the tail light.
The scooter gets a tri-tone finish with a dark brown seat and brown inner panels. This combination looks premium and pleasing.
The Ivory Elite Green has pastel green colour on the apron, front fender and side panels, and the remaining panels get ivory shade with the same dark brown seat and brown inner panels.
In the green colour, the scooter looks subtle and has a fresh, calming vibe.
The Jupiter 125 just gets a cosmetic update and doesn't see any other change.
The SmartXonnect variant can be had in Elite Green, Elegant Red, or Matte Copper Bronze; all single-tone shades
The base Drum variant is available in Indiblue, Titanium Grey, and White, while the Disc variant additionally gets Sparkling Black.

pages.title: Skoda India has started deliveries for the Kylaq and we have got you the Signature Plus in 10 images
pages.meta_description: Skoda Kylaq Signature Plus In 10 Images
headings: Skoda India has started deliveries for the Kylaq and we have got you the Signature Plus in 10 images
Pricing Range: The Signature Plus variant is priced between Rs 11.4 lakh (manual) and Rs 12.4 lakh (automatic) ex-showroom
Exterior Highlights: Retains Skoda's signature butterfly grille, LED DRLs, Candy White shade, 16-inch silver alloy wheels, and thick black body cladding
Interior Design: Features dual-tone fabric upholstery, chrome-accented dashboard, leatherette 2-spoke steering wheel, and practical additions like front and rear armrests

Feature Highlights: Equipped with a 10.1-inch infotainment system, wireless Android Auto/Apple CarPlay, auto-foldable ORVMs, and rear AC vents, but misses features like a panoramic sunroof and wireless charging
Safety Credentials: Boasts a 5-star BNCAP safety rating, and standard safety features, but lacks rain-sensing wipers and an anti-theft alarm compared to the top variant
Powertrain: Powered by a 1.0L 3-cylinder turbo petrol engine delivering 115 PS and 178 Nm, paired with either a 6-speed manual or automatic gearbox
Fuel Efficiency: Delivers an impressive mileage of 19.65 kmpl (manual) and 19.05 kmpl (automatic)
Competitive Rivals: Faces stiff competition from models like the Maruti Suzuki Brezza, Hyundai Venue, Tata Nexon, Kia Sonet, and Mahindra XUV 3X0
Appeal: Positioned as a strong value offering with a premium Skoda design ethos, suitable for buyers seeking a mid-range compact SUV

pages.title: Kia Syros Review In 10 Images
pages.meta_description: Kia India is gearing up for the launch of its premium sub-4m SUV and we’ve summed up the review in 10 images
headings: Purpose-Built for India: The Syros is designed with a compact footprint, maximizing practicality, features, and value
Quirky Design: The concept-car-like design elements make it stand out, though some elements may pose practical challenges
Maximized Space: Built on the Sonet's K1 platform, it offers a stretched wheelbase and more height
Premium Interiors: The dashboard, materials, and features, like the new two-spoke steering wheel, deliver a premium feel beyond its price point
Rear-Seat Versatility: Adjustable rear seats offer great knee room
Feature-Packed: High-end features include a panoramic sunroof, front and rear seat ventilation, 12.3-inch displays, Harman/Kardon audio, etc.
Balanced Engines: The 1-litre turbo petrol and 1.5-litre diesel engines offer adequate performance and efficiency
Ride and Handling: While easy to drive with light steering, its suspension struggles over bad roads, and high-speed ride comfort could be improved
Safety Suite: Equipped with six airbags, ABS with EBD, ESC, and advanced driver-assistance features
Value Proposition: The Syros redefines small cars by offering space without compromise, though the ride quality could be a dealbreaker

pages.title: Skoda launched the Kylaq, its contender for the sub-4m segment. We tell you the Top 10 things about the Skoda Kylaq that you should know about!
pages.meta_description: Skoda launched the Kylaq, its contender for the sub-4m segment. We tell you the Top 10 things about the Skoda Kylaq that you should know about!
headings: Segment Debut: The Kylaq marks Skoda’s entry into India’s competitive sub-4m SUV segment.
Variants & Pricing: Available in 4 variants, prices range from Rs 7.89 lakh to Rs 14.4 lakh (ex-showroom).
Engine & Transmission: Powered by a 1.0-litre turbo petrol engine (115 PS/178 Nm) with 6-speed manual and automatic transmission options.
Safety: Boasts a 5-star BNCAP safety rating with 6 airbags as standard, ESP, hill-hold control, TPMS, and more.
Top Features: Includes a 10.1-inch infotainment touchscreen, powered co-passenger seat, ventilated front seats, and wireless charging.
Interior & Comfort: Features a dual-tone dashboard, ambient lighting, standing infotainment system, and a spacious cabin with a 446-litre boot.
Dimensions: Stands at 3995 mm in length with a 2566 mm wheelbase, offering ample legroom and practicality.
Colours: Available in 7 shades – Lava Blue, Olive Gold, Candy White, Tornado Red, Deep Black, Brilliant Silver, and Carbon Steel.
Competition: Rivals include Maruti Brezza, Tata Nexon, Hyundai Venue, Kia Sonet, Mahindra XUV 3X0, and Kia Syros.
Launch & Popularity: Deliveries start today, i.e. on January 27, 2025, with 10,000 bookings secured within 10 days of opening.

## Must Know about Electric Bikes

- ### Types Of Battery The battery pack is the heart of any electric vehicle. There are two major types of batteries: Lithium-ion and Lead Acid. As the name suggests, lithium-ion battery packs use lithium as the primary compound at the positive electrode while the negative electrode is usually made out of graphite. These batteries have a higher charge density, low self-discharge levels, and are generally lighter than lead acid batteries. They also offer better range and faster charging capabilities, but come at a higher cost. The Ather 450X is a perfect example of an electric two-wheeler powered by a lithium-ion battery pack. The first rechargeable batteries to have ever been created are in fact lead acid batteries. Modern electric vehicles use Valve Regulated Lead Acid batteries (VRLA), wherein the lead electrodes are suspended in a gel-like electrolyte.

page_chunks.title: Best Electric Bikes in India 2026 - Prices, Range & Reviews | ZigWheels (part 12)
page_chunks.content:
## Must Know about Electric Bikes

These batteries are less expensive to make but their charge density isn’t as good as lithium-ion ones, so the range offered is relatively lesser. They are also heavier and take longer to charge. A prime example of an electric scooter powered by a VRLA battery is the Hero Electric Optima LX.
- ### Types Of Motors The energy stored in the battery is translated into motion using an electric motor. There are two major types of electric motors: Hub and Frame-mounted. The brushless DC hub motors, in particular, are used in most of the electric two-wheelers. They are fairly easy to install, do not require transmission components, and are affordable to manufacture as well. However, they result in an increased unsprung weight, which negatively impacts the handling of a two-wheeler. The TVS iQube Electric is a great example for an electric scooter with a hub motor.

page_chunks.title: Best Electric Bikes in India 2026 - Prices, Range & Reviews | ZigWheels (part 13)
page_chunks.content:
## Must Know about Electric Bikes

Frame-mounted motors, or mid-drive motors, are mounted onto the vehicle’s frame, and are linked to a transmission drive, which is usually either a belt or sometimes a chain. These motors are powerful, and also ensure the centre of gravity is optimised in a two-wheeler. But on the flip side, they are expensive, and the transmission drives may need regular maintenance. The Ather 450X comes with a frame mounted motor.
- ### Types Of Battery Layouts Electric two-wheelers have either a fixed battery pack or a removable one. The chassis of EVs with fixed battery packs are relatively simple, and are easy to manufacture. But since they cannot be removed, the electric two-wheelers will have to be heavily dependent on charging infrastructure. The Bajaj Chetak electric scooter comes with a fixed battery pack. Two-wheelers with removable battery packs have their chassis designed in a way to accommodate easy installation and removal of the batteries.

page_chunks.title: Best Electric Bikes in India 2026 - Prices, Range & Reviews | ZigWheels (part 14)
page_chunks.content:
## Must Know about Electric Bikes

This increases the engineering complexity, and thereby ends up increasing the manufacturing costs. But the biggest advantage is the ability to simply remove the battery pack and charge it wherever convenient. The Revolt RV 400 comes with a removable battery pack, which can easily be replaced with a fresh one in minutes.
- ### Types Of Charging There are two ways to charge a battery pack. The conventional way is to simply plug the charger into a 3-pin 5A socket and let it charge overnight. While this takes a long time to charge the battery completely, it does not heat up the battery pack as the amount of current induced is low. The Hero Electric Photon HX, for example, takes 5 hours to charge completely. On the other hand, a fast-charging system sends large amounts of current into the battery pack, thus charging them up quickly. However, batteries that are compatible with fast charging systems need to have excellent thermal management to ensure their longevity.

page_chunks.title: Best Electric Bikes in India 2026 - Prices, Range & Reviews | ZigWheels (part 15)
page_chunks.content:
## Must Know about Electric Bikes

Electric bikes and scooters with fast-charging technology are expensive too. The Ather 450X uses a proprietary AC and DC combined fast-charging system that can juice up the battery in over an hour.

The upcoming Harley Davidson X440 T is expected to launch in December 2025. Q. Is speed T4 a better option than speed 400 in terms of city rides

page_chunks.title: Compare Bikes in India 2026 - Price, Mileage & Specs | ZigWheels (part 4)
page_chunks.content: Both the Triumph Speed T4 and Speed 400 are capable motorcycles offering a blend of performance and features. The Speed T4 has a liquid-cooled, 4-valve, DOHC, single-cylinder engine producing 31 PS at 7,000 rpm and 36 Nm of torque at 5,000 rpm, with a mileage of 30 kmpl and a top speed of 135 kmph. It features dual-channel ABS and an analogue-digital instrument console, making it city-friendly and easy to handle in traffic. The Speed 400, with 40 PS at 8,000 rpm and 37.5 Nm at 6,500 rpm, a top speed of 145 kmph, and similar safety features, offers higher performance, stronger suspension, and better highway capabilities. Both motorcycles are excellent choices, and the final decision depends on your budget, intended usage, and personal preferences. page_chunks.content:
## What is the average mileage of scooters?

The mileage of scooters depends on their engine displacement. The most popular scooters in India have a displacement of 110-125cc with a mileage of around 45-60kmpl.

page_chunks.title: Best Scooters / Scooty in India 2026, Top Models, Price, Mileage | ZigWheels (part 12)
page_chunks.content:
## Can we use scooters for our daily commute?

Yes, scooters can be used for daily rides to work or leisure. One of the main reasons for their success is that they don't have a manual gearbox which makes it easier to ride in traffic.

page_chunks.title: Best Scooters / Scooty in India 2026, Top Models, Price, Mileage | ZigWheels (part 13)
page_chunks.content:
## What is the maintenance cost of scooters?

Like commuter motorcycles, scooters also use simple mechanicals so the average cost of service and maintenance is under ₹1,000 for most 110-125cc scooters.

page_chunks.title: Best Scooters / Scooty in India 2026, Top Models, Price, Mileage | ZigWheels (part 14)
page_chunks.content:
## Are scooters comfortable for long distances?

By design, scooters are more suitable for city commuting and have a smaller fuel tank of 4-6 litres. However, like any other two-wheeler, you can go touring but it wouldn't be as comfortable as a touring motorcycle.

page_chunks.title: Best Scooters / Scooty in India 2026, Top Models, Price, Mileage | ZigWheels (part 15)
page_chunks.content:
## Is registration required for scooters in India?

Yes, all ICE (internal combustion engine) scooters on sale in India need to be registered and riders are required to have a valid licence.

page_chunks.title: Best Scooters / Scooty in India 2026, Top Models, Price, Mileage | ZigWheels (part 16)
page_chunks.content:
## Is a helmet required for electric scooters in India?

Yes, wearing a helmet is crucial on any two-wheeler as crashes at speeds as low as 10kmph can be fatal.

page_chunks.title: Best Scooters / Scooty in India 2026, Top Models, Price, Mileage | ZigWheels (part 17)
page_chunks.content:
## Can we use scooters in hilly areas?

Yes, scooters can be used in hilly areas, but they tend to struggle on steep roads. Even their ground clearance isn't as high as commuter bikes which can be bothersome on rough roads.

page_chunks.title: Best Scooters / Scooty in India 2026, Top Models, Price, Mileage | ZigWheels (part 18)
page_chunks.content:
## Which are the best scooters in India?

The most popular segment in India is scooters between 110cc and 125cc. The most popular scooters on sale in India are the Honda Activa, TVS NTORQ 125, Suzuki Access 125, TVS Jupiter and Yamaha RayZR 125 Fi Hybrid.

**History:**

Maruti has been the undisputed leader of the Indian automotive industry ever since its inception back in 1981. With over 19 vehicles spanning different body styles in its portfolio, there is a Maruti Suzuki car for every budget. The carmaker’s sales and service network is also unparalleled with over 3600 dealerships and 3900 service touch points spread across the country.

The first vehicle to roll off the production line in 1983 was the Maruti 800. Before that, only a couple of carmakers were present in the country, and the Maruti 800 came in as a breath of fresh air. Currently, Maruti retails its products through two different divisions: Arena and NEXA. NEXA was launched back in 2015, with the aim of providing a platform for retailing premium models, unlike the Arena division that focuses on budget-friendly offerings.

Clear your calendars and charge your phones, because the Auto Expo is coming back. The third edition of the Bharat Mobility Global Expo will take over New Delhi from February 4 to 9, 2027, and it’s shaping up to be the biggest yet. Expect over 1,750 exhibitors, 11 shows, around 10 lakh visitors, and enough new metal to keep car and bike fans busy for days.

This year’s theme is “Smarter Mobility For a Better Tomorrow”, but we know you’re coming for the shiny new launches. Here’s everything you need to know before you plan your visit.

The expo runs from February 4 to 9, 2027. Day one is for media and industry folks only, so the public can visit from February 5. Pick your day wisely, because weekends at the Expo are famously busy.

page_chunks.title: Auto Expo 2027 Dates Out: Tickets, Venues, Expected Cars And Bikes  - ZigWheels (part 2)
page_chunks.content:
This time the action is split across two venues. The main event, the Auto Expo Motor Show, takes over Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan, from February 4 to 9, while Yashobhoomi in Dwarka runs from February 4 to 7.

If you care more about components, construction machines or flying taxis than the latest SUV, head to Dwarka before it wraps up early.

Entry was free in 2025, but this time you’ll need a ticket. It still costs less than a decent multiplex outing:

February 4: Media and industry only

Weekdays: Rs 300 per person, 10 AM to 7 PM

Weekends: Rs 200 per person, 10 AM to 6 PM

Visitor registration will open on the official Bharat Mobility Global Expo website, so keep an eye on it.

The Bharat Mobility Global Expo is more than a motor show. Bharat Mandapam will host the Auto Expo Motor Show, the India International Tyre Show, the Bharat Battery Show, the India Cycle Show, a Mobility Tech Pavilion and a Steel Pavilion.

page_chunks.title: Auto Expo 2027 Dates Out: Tickets, Venues, Expected Cars And Bikes  - ZigWheels (part 3)
page_chunks.content:
Over at Yashobhoomi, you’ll find the Components & Technology Show, the Bharat Construction Equipment Expo, the Air Mobility Expo, the Agri Mobility & Technology Expo and the Metro & Urban Mass Transit Expo.

At least 44 automakers have signed up for the Motor Show, and the confirmed list is a who’s who of Indian roads. Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai, Tata Motors, Mahindra, Kia, Toyota, Honda, Renault, MG, BYD, VinFast, BMW and Mercedes-Benz will all be there.

Hyundai could bring its biggest launch yet, the next-generation Creta. India’s favourite midsize SUV is expected to get a fresh design and a new cabin, and Hyundai might also tease its upcoming sub-compact electric SUV. Kia could hit back with the next-gen Sonet, while Maruti Suzuki may roll out its YMC electric MPV, a clear sign that family EVs are about to go mainstream.

page_chunks.title: Auto Expo 2027 Dates Out: Tickets, Venues, Expected Cars And Bikes  - ZigWheels (part 4)
page_chunks.content:
Toyota might give the Fortuner a fresh look with a facelift and bring along an updated Taisor. Renault could make this its big comeback with the Bigster and Bridger SUVs. Tata Motors could preview the next-gen Nexon and the Safari EV, both of which are expected to launch in early 2027. Mercedes-Benz, BMW and BYD are likely to fill their stands with EVs and concepts.

Major two-wheeler manufacturers expected to participate include Ather, TVS, Hero MotoCorp, Suzuki, Yamaha, Greaves Mobility and VinFast.

BMW Motorrad could showcase the F 450 R and F 450 RR, while Hero MotoCorp might bring the recently unveiled Xpulse 450 and its Vida electric motorcycle concepts. Suzuki could display an updated Avenis, whereas Yamaha might showcase the Tenere 400 concept, which was recently seen at EICMA 2026.

page_chunks.title: Auto Expo 2027 Dates Out: Tickets, Venues, Expected Cars And Bikes  - ZigWheels (part 5)
page_chunks.content:
TVS, despite unveiling the RTR 125 concept at EICMA, is unlikely to showcase it here, as the bike is primarily developed for European markets. Among EV manufacturers, Ather could display more variants of its electric scooters, while VinFast might showcase its recently patented electric motorcycle and scooter.

The dates are locked, the venues are bigger, and the line-up looks loaded. The next-gen Creta and Sonet are set to shake up India’s busiest SUV segments, and BMW’s F 450 twins and Hero’s Xpulse 450 promise a proper fight in the 450cc space. Add EV concepts, 11 shows and a bigger components hall, and Rs 300 starts to look like a bargain.

Wear comfortable shoes, carry a power bank, and stay tuned to ZigWheels for live updates and every launch from the show floor.

page_chunks.content:

- Sep 18, 2026
- Views : 1228

One flooded basement, one highway pile-up, one electrical fire. That is all it takes for a car you have loved for years to turn into a claim file. And in that moment, the single number that decides whether you walk away with a new set of keys or a hole in your savings is one most owners never look at during renewal: the car's insured value.

In India, that number is called the Insured Declared Value, or IDV. It quietly sets the ceiling on what your insurer pays for severe damage and shapes whether your car gets fixed, written off, or replaced. Here is how it works, and why getting it right matters far more than saving a few hundred rupees on premium.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 2)
page_chunks.content:
Here's the bit nobody reads at renewal. Your car's insured value, or IDV, is the maximum your insurer will ever pay if the car is stolen or written off. Not the showroom price you haggled over. Not what the used-car guy offers you. It's a formula-driven number that sits somewhere in between, and it shrinks every single year.

IDV is the manufacturer's listed selling price minus age-based depreciation under IRDAI norms. Aftermarket goodies count only if you declare them separately, and once the policy is issued, the number is locked in for the full term—no second chances mid-year.

Watch how quickly the depreciation schedule eats into a car with a Rs 10 lakh ex-showroom price:

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 3)
page_chunks.content:
| **Age of the car** | **Depreciation applied to IDV** | **IDV on a Rs 10 lakh car** |
| Up to 6 months | 5 percent | Rs 9.5 lakh |
| 6 months to 1 year | 15 percent | Rs 8.5 lakh |
| 1 to 2 years | 20 percent | Rs 8 lakh |
| 2 to 3 years | 30 percent | Rs 7 lakh |
| 3 to 4 years | 40 percent | Rs 6 lakh |
| 4 to 5 years | 50 percent | Rs 5 lakh |
| Above 5 years | Mutually agreed by insurer and owner | Based on condition and market value |

*Source: depreciation rates as per IRDAI norms*

So why lose sleep over it? Because IDV wears two hats. It determines the premium you pay today and the biggest cheque you can ever receive tomorrow. Most owners obsess over the first and completely forget the second, a mistake you usually discover only once, standing next to a crumpled car.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 4)
page_chunks.content:
Once the tow truck drives off with your car, the claim follows a fairly predictable script. You inform the insurer, a licensed surveyor arrives with a clipboard, and they assess the damage part by part. That inspection ends in one of two verdicts, and they could not be further apart.

It's repairable (partial loss): The car heads to the workshop, parts are fixed or swapped, and the insurer pays the bill minus parts depreciation, the compulsory deductible and anything excluded. You eventually get your car back.

It's not worth fixing (constructive total loss): The car is written off. No repairs, just a lump-sum payout, and you're back to car shopping.

A write-off also comes with homework. According to Section 55 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the owner of a car damaged beyond use must inform the registering RTO within 14 days so the registration can be cancelled.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 5)
page_chunks.content:
Here's the twist most owners miss: your car's verdict, and how much money follows it, both trace straight back to that one IDV figure on your policy.

In a total loss, IDV stops being a line in the policy schedule and becomes the actual cheque. Under the policy, a car is a constructive total loss when repair costs exceed 75 per cent of the IDV, and the claim settles at that agreed IDV minus the deductible. Depreciation isn't applied again, but it has already done its damage by shrinking the IDV in the first place.

So IDV pulls double duty. It sets the tripwire for a write-off and caps the payout. A car insured for Rs 6 lakh is written off once repairs hit Rs 4.5 lakh, and the owner walks away with at most Rs 6 lakh, no matter what the same car costs on-road at the dealership that week.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 6)
page_chunks.content:
That gap is exactly why the Return to Invoice (RTI) add-on exists. According to RTI, it pays up to the car's invoice value, plus first-time registration charges and road tax, if the car is stolen or written off. Here's how the two stack up:

| **What you get in a total loss** | **Standard policy** | **Policy with Return to Invoice add-on** |
| Basis of payout | Insured Declared Value (IDV) | Original invoice value of the car |
| Road tax and registration | Not covered | Reimbursed |
| Impact of age-based depreciation | Fully reflected in payout | Gap between IDV and invoice is bridged |
| Best suited to | Older cars | New cars, typically in their first few years |

Bottom line: the IDV you click 'confirm' on at renewal is the IDV you'll be paid against on the worst day of your car's life. Choose like it matters, because it does.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 7)
page_chunks.content:
Yes, and usually by far more than you saved. Dialling down the IDV at renewal feels like a clever little hack because the premium quote drops instantly. The bill for that hack only arrives when the car is stolen or totalled.

It out with a three-year-old Maruti Suzuki Swift VXi bought for Rs 7 lakh, whose IDV after 30percent depreciation comes to Rs 4.9 lakh:

| **IDV chosen** | **Indicative premium** | **Maximum payout in total loss or theft** |
| Rs 4,00,000 (lowered to save premium) | Rs 8,500 | Rs 4,00,000 |
| Rs 4,90,000 (in line with market value) | Rs 10,500 | Rs 4,90,000 |
| Rs 5,50,000 (set higher) | Rs 12,000 | Rs 5,50,000 |

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 8)
page_chunks.content:
Now do the maths on that first row. Save Rs 2,000 on premium, lose Rs 90,000 of payout. That's a terrible trade by any measure. If the Swift is written off, the owner has to dig Rs 90,000 out of savings just to get back into a similar car. With a car loan running, a reduced payout might not even cover the EMIs, leaving you paying for a car that no longer exists.

Going the other way isn't a free pass either. IDV well above realistic market value raises the premium without matching benefit and can trigger disputes at claim time. The sweet spot is boring but correct: an IDV that mirrors what your car is genuinely worth.

Accurate valuation is what turns a write-off from a financial gut-punch into a manageable reset. When the IDV truly reflects your car, the payout lands close to what it takes to put a comparable car back in your driveway. A handful of details make all the difference.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 9)
page_chunks.content:
Declare every accessory; non-factory fitted accessories count toward IDV only if you declare them separately. The insurer can’t see the touchscreen, alloy set, or CNG kit unit on the policy.

Use the flexibility you're given. Insurers let you set IDV within an approved band at purchase or renewal. Picking the realistic upper end instead of the bargain-basement floor keeps your payout honest.

Re-check when your car changes brackets. Moving from year two to year three bumps IDV depreciation from 20 percent to 30 percent, so that renewal deserves a proper look, not a lazy auto-renew.

Match add-ons to your car's age. Return to Invoice guards new cars against the IDV gap, while zero depreciation protects repair bills on partial damage.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 10)
page_chunks.content:
This is where picking the right Car Insurance policy helps. A comprehensive plan that lets you customise IDV, add accessories, and stack covers such as Return to Invoice and zero depreciation puts you in control of what you'll actually recover; for instance, it lets owners set their IDV within the permitted range online and offers cashless repairs at 10,000+ network garages, so a partial-damage claim doesn't drain your bank account while the car is being fixed.

Here's something few owners realise: the total-loss trigger is a percentage of IDV, so two owners of the same car can walk away from the same crash with completely different outcomes. The repair bill doesn't change. Only the IDV does.

Picture a car with a surveyor's repair estimate of Rs 4 lakh:

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 11)
page_chunks.content:
| **IDV on the policy** | **Repair cost as  percent of IDV** | **Likely outcome** | **What the owner ends up with** |
| Rs 5 lakh | 80 percent | Constructive total loss (above 75 percent) | Up to Rs 5 lakh, minus deductible; the car is surrendered |
| Rs 6 lakh | About 67 percent | Repaired under the policy | The same car back, repaired, minus parts depreciation and deductible |

*Calculation based on the 75 percent of IDV total-loss threshold .*

Neither outcome is automatically better. If you love your well-kept car, or own something that's tricky to replace, you'd probably rather have it fixed. If you're nursing an older car with a tired drivetrain, a clean payout might feel like a blessing. The point is that a realistic IDV keeps that call tied to your car's real condition, instead of an artificially low number shoving a perfectly repairable car into the scrapyard.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 12)
page_chunks.content:
And there's no undo button. Once a car is declared a total loss, its registration is cancelled, and it's off to the salvage yard. Better to get the number right before the accident than argue about it after.

Depreciation hits your claim twice, and owners often mix the two up. The first is yearly depreciation that shrinks your IDV and caps total-loss payouts. The second is depreciation on individual parts, which nibbles away at what the insurer pays for repairs. Major damage that stops just short of a write-off gets hit by the second one, and that's where it really stings.

According to IRDAI rates published by, here's what gets knocked off parts during a claim:

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 13)
page_chunks.content:
| **Part type** | **Depreciation deducted from claim** |
| Rubber, nylon and plastic parts | 50 percent |
| Fibreglass components | 30 percent |
| Glass | Nil |
| Paint | 50 percent on material cost of painting |
| Metal parts, car up to 6 months old | Nil |
| Metal parts, 2 to 3 years old | 15 percent |
| Metal parts, 4 to 5 years old | 35 percent |
| Metal parts, 5 to 10 years old | 40 percent |

Now look at a modern car. Bumpers, cladding, grilles, and headlamp housings are mostly plastic so that a big frontal hit can trigger a 50 percent deduction on a large chunk of the bill. Insurance gives the example of a Rs 20,000 repair where Rs 6,000 vanishes to depreciation, leaving a Rs 14,000 payout without cover versus the full Rs 20,000 with a zero depreciation add-on. Scale that up to a major-damage bill running into lakhs, and the shortfall becomes serious money.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 14)
page_chunks.content:
The takeaway: IDV decides how much you get when the car is gone; zero depreciation decides how much you keep when it's fixed. A properly protected owner needs both pulling in the same direction.

Electric cars play by slightly different rules because a big chunk of their value sits in one component you can't see or easily fix: the battery pack. The battery is the most expensive part of an EV, and its value directly drives the premium. Motor repairs and other EV-specific hardware can also cost more than equivalent work on a petrol or diesel car.

That shakes up the IDV maths in three big ways:

Total loss can arrive sooner. If a flooded underpass or a nasty underbody hit damages the pack, the repair estimate alone can quickly reach the 75 percent of IDV threshold, especially on a car that's a few years old. An EV can be written off after damage that would only mean a long workshop stay for a petrol car.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 15)
page_chunks.content:
An undervalued IDV hurts more. With so much value packed into the battery and power electronics, a low IDV leaves an even wider hole between your payout and the cost of a replacement.

Standard cover can miss EV bits. Standard policies usually don't cover home charging units and cables, and they cover battery damage only when caused by an insured event, not gradual wear.

| **Factor** | **Petrol or diesel car** | **Electric car** |
| Single most expensive component | Engine and gearbox | Battery pack, the costliest part of an EV |
| Typical major-damage risk | Engine hydrolock in floods, body damage | Battery and electrical damage from water ingress or underbody impact |
| Chance of a repair bill crossing 75 percent of IDV | Lower, spread across many parts | Higher, concentrated in the battery |
| Extra cover worth considering | Engine protection, zero depreciation | EV-specific add-on for battery and charger, zero depreciation, Return to Invoice |

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 16)
page_chunks.content:
Which is why EV owners should treat Electric Car Insurance as its own animal, not a copy-paste of a petrol-car policy. An EV-specific plan lets you set an IDV that reflects the battery's share of the car's value and adds protection standard cover leaves out. The EV Shield add-on covers loss or damage to the battery, charging cable, charger, and the charging point's electrical panel, plus battery-related roadside assistance, so one bad monsoon evening doesn't turn into a crippling battery bill.

Five minutes with your policy schedule before you hit 'renew' can decide how the worst-case scenario plays out. Here's your pre-renewal checklist:

The IDV figure itself - Compare it with what similar cars of your model, variant and year are actually selling for. If the IDV is well below that, nudge it up within the band your insurer allows.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 17)
page_chunks.content:
Declared accessories and fitments - Make sure aftermarket additions such as a CNG kit, music system or alloy wheels are listed, or they will not count in a total-loss payout.

Your car's depreciation bracket - Check whether the car has just moved into a new age slab, since IDV and parts depreciation both step up at those points.

Return to Invoice eligibility - For a car in its early years, check whether RTI is available and worth adding to close the gap between IDV and the on-road price.

Zero depreciation and its claim limit - Confirm it is active and note how many claims per year it covers, since insurers point out that standard depreciation applies once that limit is used up.

Outstanding loan versus IDV - If the car is financed, make sure the IDV is not lower than what you still owe the lender.

EV-specific protection - For electric cars, confirm whether the battery, charger and charging cable are covered, and add an EV-focused add-on if they are not.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 18)
page_chunks.content:
Policy type - A third-party-only policy pays nothing for your own car, so major damage cover needs a comprehensive or standalone own-damage plan.

We'll be honest: IDV is the most underrated number in Indian car ownership. We'll happily spend a weekend debating two variants over a Rs 20,000 difference, then accept whatever IDV the renewal page throws at us without a second glance. That's backwards.

Our take is simple. If your car is under three years old, pair a realistic IDV with Return to Invoice and zero depreciation, because the gap between IDV and on-road price is widest right then. If your car is older, resist the urge to slash IDV for a cheaper quote; the couple of thousand rupees you save is pocket change next to the payout you give up. And if you drive an EV, don't assume a regular policy covers your battery. Check and add EV-specific protection if it doesn't.

page_chunks.title: Car Insurance IDV Explained: Depreciation, Total Loss & Payouts  - ZigWheels (part 19)
page_chunks.content:
Insurance is the one purchase you hope never to use. But when you do need it, the IDV you picked months earlier decides whether that bad day ends with a fresh start or a financial headache. Set it right once a year. Your future self, standing beside a crumpled bonnet, will thank you.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 1)
page_chunks.content:
Maruti Finally Launches AMT for Dzire, Baleno, Swift S-CNG! Now Worry...

- Sep 18, 2026
- Views : 1228

A used car that appears to be good in photos and even better in person can still turn into an expensive mistake. Buyers feel they've found a great deal once they negotiate a few thousand rupees off the asking price, and then skip the major checks they should do. They skip the checks that reveal whether the car has been in an accident, whether it still has a loan against it, or whether the papers even match the vehicle sitting in front of you.

To make things simpler, we have a detailed inspection guide that will make you a pro at inspecting cars. Here's a step-by-step way to inspect any used car properly, from paperwork to delivery day.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 2)
page_chunks.content:
Before driving the car, you should check the papers thoroughly. The registration certificate (RC) should align with the chassis number that has been stamped on the car. Depending on the make and model, this number is stamped on the firewall, the boot floor, or the B-pillar, and it should look factory-original, not recently stamped.

Another important step is to cross-check everything on the VAHAN portal: pending challans, insurance validity, and whether the car is hypothecated to a bank.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 3)
page_chunks.content: Buyers end up treating paperwork as a formality when the seller is friendly or someone you might know through a close friend. But paperwork is often the first place fraud shows up, so working through it methodically, the way a proper PDI checklist for used cars would have you do, is worth the extra time that you would have to invest. Don't stop at checking whether insurance is active, but ask for the vehicle’s insurance claim history. This will give you a far better picture of the car's past than the policy document alone.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 4)
page_chunks.content:
If the car was financed, the loan needs to be fully cleared before you go any further. Ask for the clearance letter along with Form 35, and make sure Forms 29 and 30 are in order for the ownership transfer. In some cases, buyers really like a car from another state, and in this case, your buying process gets a bit more layered: you'll need a No Objection Certificate from the original RTO, and that process can take a few weeks, so it's not something to leave until the last moment.

A car’s paint does not always tell the truth, even when the seller is trying to. A paint thickness gauge is one of the most useful tools you can carry, and a decent one costs less than filling up a tank of fuel. Factory paint stays within a fairly tight thickness range across the entire car. Paint consistency should be checked here; that is, if one door or a quarter panel reads noticeably different from the rest, that panel has been repainted.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 5)
page_chunks.content:
Next, check the fasteners. Bolts on the fender and bonnet hinges will show scratch marks if they've ever been removed. Panel gaps should be even and consistent all the way from the headlight to the taillight; anywhere that gap changes, something has been taken off and refitted. A slight mismatch in panel gaps is fine, as some new cars also have these gaps. However, if the difference is a lot, then you should take note of it.

Lifting the boot carpet and checking the spare wheel well for ripples or fresh welding is one of the most important steps that buyers miss out on. It's one of the clearest signs of a rear-end repair. Rubber door seals should also show uniform ageing across the car. A seal that looks newer than the rest usually means that door has a story behind it.

Never ignore the tyres. On the sidewall, there is a DOT code stamped, which tells you exactly when each tyre was manufactured. This is reliable proof about how well the car has actually been maintained.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 6)
page_chunks.content:
Always remember to do a cold start, standing in front with the bonnet open. A cold start exposes problems a warm engine conveniently hides. A cold start can show you the car’s true colours, with common problems being tappet noise, injector chatter, turbo whine, or blue smoke on startup. If a seller insists the car is "already warmed up," that's not a favour; that's damage control or simply trying to lock the deal by hiding the real problem.

So you have now turned on the car and checked for unwanted sounds. Your next step shouldn’t be to drive right away. You should plug in an OBD scanner and check for stored fault codes, not just the ones currently active. It's also worth asking directly whether the fault code memory has been cleared recently, since that alone can hide a lot.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 7)
page_chunks.content:
Once that is done, it is time to finally drive the car. Once you start driving, try to pay attention to the minor but significant details. Observe if the car pulls to one side under braking, or if the shift from second to third gear happens cleanly, and whether the clutch bite point feels unusually high or low. For better observations, roll the windows down, turn the music off, and drive over a rough patch of road since suspension knocks are far easier to notice when there is less noise.

Even after you've decided to buy, the inspection isn't over. Check that both keys are present, along with the spare wheel, jack, toolkit, and the original owner's manual. Ensure to take photographs of the car from all four corners before you drive off, so there's a clear record of its condition at handover.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 8)
page_chunks.content:
For a brand-new car, the checks are slightly different but just as important: verify the manufacturing date, look closely for any transit damage, check for leftover protective film residue, and confirm every dealer-fitted accessory matches what was actually ordered. A proper pre-delivery inspection checklist for a new car essentially comes down to five things: Paint thickness, panel gaps, the undercarriage, the engine bay, and the electronics. Get those right, and there's very little left to surprise you later.

So whether it is a used car or a new car, there can be some unwanted issues.

Pro tip: If there are minor scratches on a new car, you can ask the dealer for a bigger discount or free scratch repair. Similarly, for a used car, your thorough check can help you negotiate the price of the car if you really like that particular car and want it irrespective of the minor issues.

page_chunks.title: The Complete Used Car Inspection Guide: Check Out The Most Essential Steps Of Buying A Used Car  - ZigWheels (part 9)
page_chunks.content:
A used car deal is only as good as the checks you actually bother to do. A bit more effort and research today will ensure that you pick the right car and you will have more peace of mind in the future. You may sometimes get too excited dreaming about the delivery day and taking your loved ones out for a drive, but it is important to think rationally first and ensure that you do not miss out on any of the checkpoints mentioned above. None of these checks takes more than a few minutes each, but skipping even one is how buyers end up with a car that still owes the bank money, or a repair bill they didn't see coming. Do the homework upfront, and the car you drive home will be exactly what it looked like on paper.

Let us know in the comments section if you have any more questions regarding car inspection.

## Sierra Pros and Cons

**Good Things**

- Stunning (Red Dot award-winning) design and road presence. Grabs attention even before you know it’s called Sierra.
- Good range of engines and transmissions to choose from. Turbo-petrol is exciting!
- Top-notch safety: Up to 7 airbags, ESC, Level 2 ADAS, high-resolution 360 degree camera and more.
- Tech-bomb! Triple screens, BIG panoramic sunroof, 12-speaker JBL Black sound system, front seat ventilation, and more.
- Plenty spacious and practical for the family’s use. Backseat owners will love the space, comfort and amenities.
- Big boot can easily handle road trips or airport runs.
- Great ride quality. Feels planted and ready for rough roads

**Could be Better**

- The front row is not spacious for exceptionally tall users (over 6.2-6.3ft). Most rivals in the segment are more accommodating for such drivers/passengers.
- Issues and niggles experienced such as loose trim and glitching electronics.
- Diesel engine refinement could be better

## About Tata

**History**

Part of the gigantic Tata group founded by Jamsetji Tata in 1868, Tata Motors is one of the leading Indian car manufacturers. Established in 1945, Tata Motors' diverse portfolio includes an extensive range of cars, sport utility vehicles, trucks, buses and defence vehicles. Jaguar and Land Rover; the two prestigious British car brands were acquired by Tata back in 2008.

Tata launched the Tata Indica in 1998; its first passenger car in India, which paved the way for the future models to come. Tata (Telco back then) was also responsible for bringing the three-pointed star (Mercedes-Benz) to India in 1995.

**Product portfolio**

Hatchback: Tata's hatchbacks' portfolio ranges from the Tiago and Tiago EV to the Altroz.

Micro SUV: Tata offers the Punch and Punch EV as entry-level micro SUVs. It takes on the Mahindra Exter and Maruti Fronx but due to its price, it also rivals the Nissan Magnite and Renault Kiger.

## About Kia

**History**

Korean automaker Kia has a long history of producing global cars for sale in Europe and other countries. It started out in 1944 as a bicycle manufacturer and graduated to producing cars in the 1980s. Since then, it has become a globally renowned carmaker under its parent company, Hyundai.

Kia Motors set up a manufacturing facility to build cars in India in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh, in 2017. It has been in India for barely seven years, but already, it's a mainstream carmaker with multiple models on sale. The Seltos was Kia's debut car in 2019, based on the SP2 SUV concept that was globally unveiled in India at Auto Expo 2018. It was launched in the lucrative compact SUV segment that allowed Kia to price the car well in India. Since then, the automaker has introduced vehicles at multiple price points – a full-size people carrier, a more affordable alternative to the Seltos, the smaller Sonet SUV, the Syros subcompact SUV, and a smaller MPV.

People carriers: The Carnival was Kia's first people mover in India. It can seat anywhere from 7 to 9 people, and it slots above the Toyota Innova in the market. In late 2021 Kia introduced a 'recreational vehicle' (RV), the Carens three-row people carrier, followed by the Carens Clavis in 2025.

## About Hyundai

**History**

Incorporated in 1996, Hyundai Motor India Limited (HMIL) is a wholly owned subsidiary of South Korea's Hyundai Motor Company (HMC). Hyundai currently has two manufacturing plants in India, located at Irungattukottai and Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu, with an annual combined production capacity of 7.65 lakh units a year. In 1998, the Korean manufacturer began manufacturing the Santro followed by its launch. The carmaker is known for its diverse product portfolio and a wide service station network. It is the second largest carmaker in the country by volume and also one of the largest exporters.

**Product portfolio**

Hatchbacks: Hyundai has a varied lineup of hatchbacks – right from affordable models like the Grand i10 Nios to sportier versions of the i20 and the i20 N Line.

## About Mahindra

**History**

Mahindra is an Indian automaker that has been building cars, primarily SUVs, for the subcontinent ever since the first Willys Jeeps arrived in the 1950s. It has a legacy of building tough, diesel-powered utility vehicles, such as the CJ-series Jeeps and the Thar. Mahindra’s cars have always been popular people movers in India for the value they offer in their go-anywhere capability and price.

Four-wheel drive lies at the roots of Mahindra’s history -- it started out by assembling 4x4 Willy’s Jeeps and later developed its own off-roading vehicles and hardware such as transmissions and transfer cases. Over the years Mahindra has given us a score of memorable and capable off-roaders and family SUVs in India, at different price points across multiple segments.

**Product portfolio**

Micro SUV: Mahindra offers the KUV100 NXT micro-SUV in India. It’s a raised-up hatchback with an 82PS 1.2-litre petrol engine that rivals the Maruti Suzuki Ignis.

People movers: Legacy Mahindra models have long served as a staple in rural areas where they are still used as people carriers. Nowadays, the carmaker offers the Marazzo MPV in 6- and 7-seater layouts as a relatively premium rival to the Maruti Suzuki Ertiga.

## About Skoda

History

Czech carmaker Skoda Auto has its roots tracing back to over 120 years. It started making vehicles in the 1930s, but in 1991, it became a subsidiary of the Volkswagen Group.

Skoda began its operations in India in late 2001, and launched its first car, the Octavia sedan, in 2002. It was initially imported in semi knock-down kits and assembled locally in the country. Now Skoda’s Aurangabad facility is a full-fledged manufacturing plant.

With the India 2.0 Project, the carmaker has implemented the highly localised MQB A0-IN vehicle platform. As the name suggests, it is an iteration of the global MQB A0 platform where all upcoming models will be designed and manufactured locally.

Since 2019, Skoda India has been operated under Skoda Auto Volkswagen India Private Limited, a subsidiary of the global VW Group undertaking the business activities of five brands in India: Skoda, Audi, Volkswagen, Porsche, and Lamborghini.

**History:**

Founded by Louis Renault and his brothers, Renault is a French automaker established in 1898.

Renault came to India in 2005, but it wasn’t until 2007 that it launched its first car in the country, the Renault Logan. In 2010, the Renault-Nissan alliance set up a manufacturing facility in Chennai, which was completed in a record 21 months, and is capable of producing 480,000 vehicles annually. Renault has more than 525 sales and 530 service touchpoints in India, including 250+ Workshop On Wheels or mobile workshops across the country.

The French marque also has a prestigious motorsport heritage - not only is it one of the handful brands to compete in Formula 1, it’s also one of the most decorated ones; winning two constructors' and drivers' championships, while as an engine manufacturer it has 12 constructors' and 11 drivers' championships.

## About Renault

Renault India is known for its competitive pricing, offering budget-friendly cars that cater to the masses. Currently, it has three cars in its line-up: Kwid, Triber and Kiger.

Hatchback: Launched back in 2015, the Kwid took the market by a storm. It was the first SUV-styled entry-level hatchback in the Indian market at the time. But with changing consumer preferences, the entry-level hatchback segment seems to be losing its sheen and despite numerous additions and variations, the Kwid’s dominance has seen a downfall.

Sub-compact SUV: The Kiger is Renault’s offering in the crowded sub-compact SUV segment comprising the Nissan Magnite, Kia Sonet, and even the Tata Punch micro SUV among others.

People mover: Renault’s sub-4m crossover MPV, the Triber, was launched in 2019. With modular seating options, the MPV is best suited for those wanting a versatile and budget-friendly seven-seater.

page_chunks.title: Best Hybrid Cars in India 2026 - Top Hybrid Cars, Price, Images, mileage (part 8)
page_chunks.content:
## What is the difference between hybrid cars and electric cars?

A hybrid car is essentially a middle ground between cars powered by internal combustion engines (ICE) and pure electric vehicles (EVs) that use only a battery and an electric motor. A hybrid car houses a regular engine like all ICE cars while also featuring a small battery pack and an electric motor, which comes into action during low speeds or less stress conditions. They can be driven by either the engine or the motor; or combined. Meanwhile, EVs have a large battery pack and no combustion engine at all. EVs are powered only by the battery pack, which is charged using electricity. Most hybrids sold in India use self-charging technology and don’t require to be plugged in, unlike electric cars and plug-in hybrids. The Honda City e:HEV and Maruti Grand Vitara are examples of hybrid vehicles while there isn’t a single plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) in India as of now. Some examples of EVs are the Tata Tiago EV, Kia EV6 and Audi e-tron SUV.

page_chunks.title: Best Hybrid Cars in India 2026 - Top Hybrid Cars, Price, Images, mileage (part 9)
page_chunks.content:
## What are 3 drawbacks of hybrid cars?

The 3 major drawbacks of hybrid cars are:

(i). Expensive to own due to the maintenance cost of the battery pack and powertrain compared to EVs, as the latter don/'t feature any mechanical components.

(ii). They are not as environmentally friendly as electric cars because they consist of a combustible engine, which adds to the pollution.

(iii). No incentives/subsidies on hybrid cars yet unlike EVs in India.

page_chunks.title: Best Hybrid Cars in India 2026 - Top Hybrid Cars, Price, Images, mileage (part 10)
page_chunks.content:
## What is good about hybrid cars?

Hybrid cars are less polluting than pure internal combustion engines (ICE) cars, and don/'t have the infrastructural challenges as faced by EV owners with regards to charging stations. They can run in pure EV mode at low loads and offer significantly more overall fuel economy, reducing fuel consumption all around. The battery pack is recharged by regenerative braking and also by any excess energy produced by the engine.

page_chunks.title: Best Hybrid Cars in India 2026 - Top Hybrid Cars, Price, Images, mileage (part 11)
page_chunks.content:
## What are the different types of hybrids?

There are three types of hybrid options: mild-, strong- and plug-in hybrids. While all three come with a battery pack and an electric motor on board, their battery packs vary in capacity depending on the type of hybrid chosen. It’s the mild-hybrid setup here which consists of the lowest voltage battery unit. The mild-hybrid’s battery-motor setup is used to only power the electrical components of a vehicle and to assist the engine in start/stop scenarios. It can also provide a small torque boost during acceleration at low engine speeds but cannot operate the vehicle in a ‘battery-only’ power and ‘zero-emissions’ mode. A strong-hybrid, on the other hand, powers the car using an electric motor during short distances while juicing up its battery by using either the engine or through regenerative braking. Plug-in hybrids, as the name says, can be recharged by plugging them into a home charging plug or by a public charger.

page_chunks.title: Best Hybrid Cars in India 2026 - Top Hybrid Cars, Price, Images, mileage (part 12)
page_chunks.content:
## What are the different types of hybrids?

They fit in between strong-hybrid vehicles (which get self-charging tech) and fully electric vehicles (which need to be plugged in).

## About Honda

A brief history of HMSI (Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India)

The beginnings of Honda can be traced back all the way to the end of World War II, where Soichiro Honda decided to mount a former Imperial Army generator engine to a bicycle to produce affordable and efficient mobility for the masses of war-ravaged Japan. Soon Honda became a manufacturer of bicycle auxiliary engines and in the years that followed, started producing proper world class motorcycles. But it was the 1954 Honda Super Cub that really shot the company to global acclaim. The Super Cub is important even in the Indian context as a motor derived from the Cub became the mainstay of the Japanese company’s joint venture with Hero in India.

page_chunks.title: Honda Bikes in India - Honda Models Price 2026 - Offers, Reviews & Dealers - ZigWheels (part 18)

## About Honda

Honda of Japan entered India back in 1984 with two main tie-ups. One with Hero to produce small capacity 4-stroke commuter motorcycles such as the Hero Honda CD100, which featured a “sloper” motor derived from the Cub. The other was with Pune-based Kinetic Motors to produce what would be India’s first automatic scooter, the 2-stroke Kinetic Honda DX. But the Japanese bike maker parted ways with Kinetic in 1998 and entered India as Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India, a wholly owned subsidiary of Honda Motor Company, Japan. It was then they launched their own automatic scooter, the 4-stroke Activa, which quickly became the company’s best selling bike and India’s best selling scooter, and remains so till date.

## About Honda

At the same time, HMSI also started making motorcycles, one of the most popular of which was the Honda Unicorn, and later the Honda Shine. It was in 2011 that the joint venture between Hero and Honda ended and both companies went their separate ways. While Hero continued to enjoy record breaking sales with the Splendor (originally a Hero Honda bike), it was the Activa (and also the Shine to a certain extent) that elevated HMSI to the position of 2nd largest 2-wheeler maker in India. In 2020, HMSI also took on the might of the Royal Enfield Classic 350 with their own classic motorcycle, the H’ness CB350.

Today, HMSI offers a range of Indian manufactured 110-125cc scooters, 110-350cc motorcycles and even CKD and CBU big bikes such as the CBR650R Fireblade, Africa Twin and even the mammoth tourer, the Gold Wing.

## Is Royal Enfield an Indian company?

While deeply embedded in Indian culture, Royal Enfield's roots actually trace back to 1901 England. In 1949, K. R. Sundaram Iyer launched Madras Motors to import British motorcycles into India, including Royal Enfields. In 1952, Madras Motors received an order from the Indian Army for 500 350cc Bullets. The motorcycles arrived from Redditch, UK, in early 1953 and this was really the beginning of India’s love for the Royal Enfield Bullet. It was after that, in 1955, that Royal Enfield collaborated with Madras Motors to form Enfield India to open a factory in Thiruvottiyur, Tamil Nadu to assemble Bullets from kits shipped from the UK.

page_chunks.title: Royal Enfield Bikes in India - Royal Enfield Models Price 2026 - Offers, Reviews & Dealers - ZigWheels (part 22)

## Is Royal Enfield an Indian company?

After Royal Enfield’s Redditch factory closed in 1967, Enfield India still kept manufacturing Bullets under license from Royal Enfield UK, and then later in 1977, started importing these Indian-made Bullets to the UK and Europe. In 1994, Royal Enfield was acquired by the Eicher Group, an Indian company that manufactures tractors and commercial vehicles, making it proudly Indian in ownership and operation.

Today, Royal Enfield is a global brand with a loyal following among enthusiasts and riders. The company's motorcycles are sold in over 60 countries around the world, with a growing presence in markets like the United States and Europe.

## **Origin**

TVS, a renowned name in the automotive industry, traces its roots all the way back to 1911 when its founder, T.V. Sundaram Iyengar, started a bus service company called Sundaram Iyengar and Sons Limited in Delhi. After his passing, his sons took over and in 1962, they joined forces with a UK-based company to establish Sundaram Clayton. This partnership aimed to manufacture automotive components such as motorcycle brakes and compressors. It wasn't until 1978 that TVS ventured into the production of mopeds at their plant in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, and in 1980, they introduced India's first 2-seat moped, the TVS 50.

## **Origin**

In 1982, Sundaram Clayton joined hands with Suzuki from Japan to produce two-stroke motorcycles. Models like the Supra, Samurai, Shogun, and Shaolin gained popularity in the Indian market. TVS-Suzuki also made a mark in the motorcycle racing scene with a modified version of the TVS 50 that could reach speeds of 105 kmph. When this collaboration ended in 2001, all TVS Suzuki bikes were brought under the umbrella of TVS Motors.

## **Origin**

Thanks to their extensive interest in and history with racing, TVS has been able to introduce many technological firsts in their bikes over the years. They introduced India's first fully indigenously made gearless scooter, the Scooty, the first bike with digital ignition, the Champ, and the Apache RTR, which was the first Indian-made bike with ABS. While the Scooty name still soldiers on in a couple of models, it has become synonymous with gearless scooters, it was the Jupiter 110 and more recently the Jupiter 125 which have been extremely successful in the scooter segment, outselling everything but the Honda Activa. More recently, TVS Motors forayed into the electric scooter segment with the iQube and iQube S. In the last couple of years, TVS has also tried to take on the likes of classic motorcycles like Royal Enfield with their latest bike, the Ronin.

In 2013, TVS partnered with BMW Motorrad to co-develop and produce a new 310cc platform with them to produce bikes built on this platform for the German marque, but also a brand new full-faired sport bike - the Apache RR310 as well. ## About Yamaha

When you think of Yamaha, you think of high performance motorcycles. This is not a modern trend, but has been the company’s philosophy ever since its inception back in the 1950s. In 1950, Genichi Kawakami became the 4th generation president of Nippon Gakki - a company that produced musical instruments and electronics. Kawakami decided to expand the Nippon Gakki company’s portfolio into motorcycles. For this, in 1954 Kawakami’s team of engineers made their first prototype motorcycle, the YA-1 - a 125cc single cylinder 2-stroke machine. It was a motorcycle that proved its mettle through an unprecedented 10,000km endurance test and in 1955, Yamaha Motor Co Ltd was formed along with its own factory to mass produce this motorcycle. In the proceeding years, the YA-1 won many races throughout Japan, and established Yamaha as a manufacturer of performance motorcycles.

## About Hero

Hero MotoCorp, formerly known as Hero Honda, is an Indian motorcycle and scooter manufacturer that has been in operation since 1984. The company was formed as a joint venture between Hero Cycles, one of India's largest bicycle manufacturers, and Honda Motor Company of Japan.

The partnership between Hero Cycles and Honda Motor Company was a major success, with the two companies quickly becoming the largest motorcycle manufacturers in India. The joint venture resulted in the formation of Hero Honda Motors Limited, with Hero Cycles owning a majority stake in the company.

In the years that followed, Hero Honda Motors Limited became known for producing some of the most popular motorcycles in India, including the CD 100, Splendor, and Passion. These motorcycles were known for their reliability, affordability, and fuel efficiency, and quickly became bestsellers in the Indian market.

## About Hero

In 2010, after nearly three decades of partnership, Hero Cycles and Honda Motor Company decided to end their joint venture. The split was amicable, with both companies agreeing to continue to use the "Hero" brand name and logo for a period of time.

After the split, Hero MotoCorp continued to manufacture and sell motorcycles and scooters under the Hero brand. Today, Hero MotoCorp is the largest two-wheeler manufacturer in India, with a market share of over 35%. Hero also collaborated with Speedbrain to develop a rally bike and compete in the Dakar Rally, the world’s most gruelling off-road race.

## About Bajaj

**Latest Update on Bajaj Auto**

2026 has been a busy year for Bajaj Auto. Since November 2025, the company has updated seven motorcycles, including the latest Pulsar 150 and Pulsar 125. Bajaj is also expected to introduce eight more motorcycles over the next few months, strengthening its lineup across the original Pulsar range, the NS series and the newer N series. Reports also suggest the company is working on a new sub-brand for motorcycles in the 125cc to 250cc segment. Alongside its petrol-powered models, Bajaj recently launched the Chetak C25 electric scooter with a claimed range of 113km and is developing a modular electric motorcycle platform for its upcoming EVs.

**Origins**

Bajaj Auto Limited is an Indian multinational two-wheeler and three-wheeler manufacturing company that was founded in 1945. The company was initially established as a trading company, importing and selling Vespa scooters in India under license from the Italian company Piaggio.

## About Bajaj

In 1959, Bajaj Auto began manufacturing scooters in India under its own brand name. The company's first scooter, the Bajaj Priya, was a huge success in the Indian market and was followed by other popular models like the Chetak and Super.

In the 1970s, Bajaj Auto expanded its product range to include motorcycles, introducing the Bajaj 150 and 175. These motorcycles were popular among Indian consumers, thanks to their affordability, reliability, and fuel efficiency.

In the years that followed, Bajaj Auto continued to innovate and expand its product lineup. In 1986, the company introduced the Bajaj Sunny, a scooter that was designed specifically for women. In 2002, Bajaj Auto launched the Pulsar, a sporty motorcycle that quickly became a bestseller in the Indian market.

## About Bajaj

Today, Bajaj Auto is one of the largest two-wheeler manufacturers in the world, with a wide range of motorcycles and scooters that are sold in India and in international markets. In recent years, the company has also focused on developing electric vehicles, launching the Chetak electric scooter in 2020.

In 2007, Bajaj and KTM joined hands in a strategic partnership between Bajaj Auto and KTM AG, with Bajaj Auto acquiring a 14.5% stake in KTM AG - a stake which later grew to 49.9%. The partnership has been highly successful, with the two companies collaborating on the development of new motorcycles and sharing technology and manufacturing expertise. Bajaj Auto manufactures KTM bikes in India and exports them to markets around the world, while KTM AG provides Bajaj Auto with access to its advanced technology and design capabilities. Today, the Bajaj-KTM tie-up is considered one of the most successful collaborations in the global motorcycle industry.
